Rules / Performance

SK4041 The StringBuilder is filled and never read

A local StringBuilder is constructed and appended to, and nothing in the member ever reads its text or hands it to anything that could.

CategoryPerformance
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS3063

Why

Every Append copies characters into a buffer, grows it when it runs out, and the whole of it is then collected. The work is real and the result is discarded. ⚠ It is almost never a performance mistake by intent — it is a missing line. The usual cause is a return builder.ToString(); that was never written, or a caller that was deleted while the code filling the buffer stayed; both compile, both pass every test that does not assert on the output, and neither the compiler nor the SDK analyzers say a word, because appending to a local and dropping it is legal in exactly the way appending to a local and using it is.

Example

Instead of:

void Report(IEnumerable<Entry> entries) {
    var builder = new StringBuilder();
    foreach (var entry in entries) {
        builder.AppendLine(entry.Name);
    }
}

Write:

string Report(IEnumerable<Entry> entries) {
    var builder = new StringBuilder();
    foreach (var entry in entries) {
        builder.AppendLine(entry.Name);
    }

    return builder.ToString();
}

When it does not fire

⚠ A `StringBuilder` handed to anything else escapes, and the rule stands down at the first sign of it rather than reasoning about it. A method taking one may read it, store it or return its text, and nothing in this compilation is obliged to say so. So an argument, an assignment, a return, a second local aliasing it, or any reference at all inside a lambda or a local function ends the analysis for that local. The default is "this is a read": only nine mutating members are recognised as writes, so a member added to StringBuilder in a later framework silences the rule instead of making it wrong. ⚠ `Length` and `Capacity` are reads. Setting Length truncates the buffer and is a write, and reading it is a read, and the name alone does not say which — so both are treated as reads and the rule is silent on a builder whose length is inspected. ⚠ The initializer has to be `new StringBuilder(…)`, in either the explicit or the target-typed spelling. A builder taken from a pool or a factory is shared with whoever handed it over, and "nothing in this method reads it" says nothing at all about it. ⚠ The scan covers the whole member body, not the enclosing block: a builder filled inside an if and read after it is read, and a scan that stopped at the block would report it. ⚠ No fix, and the reason is the finding. The edit that repairs this is the read that was never written, and nothing here knows what the author meant to do with the text. Deleting the builder is the other candidate and is wrong whenever an append's argument has side effects — builder.Append(Next()) — so the rule reports and stops, as SK4024 does. ⚠ Nothing in the .NET SDK reports this shape. A probe at AnalysisMode=All against the 10.0.400 SDK produced only CA1834 on the same code, which is about Append(char) versus Append(string) and fires whether or not the buffer is ever read.
